correctness.rationale: Direct differentiation of the finite geometric sum supplies the discrete Fourier coefficients for arbitrary phase; normalized Parseval gives an exact sum, uniform Riemann-sum convergence and zeta tail yield \(F(a)+O(N^{-1})\). Fourier decay \(O(k^{-2})\) yields \(L^2\) remainder \(O(N^{-3/2})\), sufficient after taking cross terms. Positive cosine defect proves strict unique minimization, and a corrected Fourier coefficient plus \(x\cot x<1\) gives the midpoint-aligned comparison. The standard-library checker passes finite diagnostics; these are not used as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Sampling phase relative to an actual jump is a natural design parameter. Determining the complete leading squared-L2 coefficient and the unique optimal half-cell placement is more informative than a coarse \(O(N^{-1/2})\) estimate, while the midpoint-aligned comparison answers an alternative jump-data convention. The theorem covers every smooth perturbation with \(O(k^{-2})\) Fourier tail uniformly in phase, without asserting multi-jump or other-grid results.
